behavioral_notes.observation: The reusable base every Odoo spreadsheet record inherits (spreadsheet.dashboard, documents.document, spreadsheet.template, etc.). It stores the o-spreadsheet workbook twice: spreadsheet_binary_data is a Binary attachment holding the JSON workbook (base64), and spreadsheet_data is a Text field that is NOT stored — it is computed (_compute_spreadsheet_data) by reading the raw bytes of the linked ir.attachment (res_field='spreadsheet_binary_data') and inverse-written (_inverse_spreadsheet_data) back into that attachment as base64. So the 'document' is an attachment blob, and the Text field is just a convenience view onto it. A fresh record defaults to _empty_spreadsheet_data(): one 'Sheet1' (translated for the creator), the user's locale, and revisionId 'START_REVISION'. This is the metadata-invisible storage contract behind every spreadsheet feature.

On write of spreadsheet_binary_data the workbook JSON is decoded and (in test mode) statically validated against the live ORM: fields_in_spreadsheet(data) walks every model/field-chain referenced by pivots, lists and ODOO formulas inside the cells and raises ValidationError if a model is unknown or a field-chain (e.g. 'product_id.channel_ids') does not resolve through relational hops; menus_xml_ids_in_spreadsheet(data) checks that every embedded ir.ui.menu xml-id exists and has an action. An xlsx blob ([Content_Types].xml present) is skipped. This means the spreadsheet's BI content is effectively a typed reference into the data model — not opaque text — but the binding lives in the JSON, not in ORM metadata.

xlsx export is assembled client-side (the o-spreadsheet JS produces the list of file parts) and only zipped server-side: _zip_xslx_files(files) streams a ZIP_DEFLATED archive, and for each part either writes its 'content' or, when only an 'imageSrc' is sent (to save bandwidth), resolves the image — base64 data: URIs are decoded directly, while /web/image/<id> paths are streamed from the backing ir.attachment via ir.binary. Embedded charts/figures thus become real image bytes inside the .xlsx. The heavy lifting (cell/format/formula serialization) is the JS engine; Python only packages.

behavioral_notes.element: /spreadsheet/log (controller) + res.currency/res.lang/ir.model helper RPCs — server-side data plumbing
behavioral_notes.observation: The only Python route here is telemetry: SpreadsheetController.log_action logs export/copy/freeze/print events, stringifying each datasource (resModel + fields + groupby + domain) for audit of what business data left the system. The substantive server surface is a set of @api.readonly @api.model helper methods the JS lib batches over standard call_kw, NOT bespoke routes: res.lang.get_locales_for_spreadsheet/_get_user_spreadsheet_locale (locale injection), res.currency.get_company_currency_for_spreadsheet + res.currency.rate.get_rates_for_spreadsheet (currency formatting & conversion for ODOO.CURRENCY.RATE), ir.model.has_searchable_parent_relation (hierarchy support), and spreadsheet.mixin.get_display_names_for_spreadsheet (batched display_name resolution for relation cells). NOTE: the collaborative edit endpoints (dispatch_spreadsheet_message / save_spreadsheet_snapshot / join_spreadsheet_session) and the /spreadsheet/data/<model>/<id> load+save routes that the JS references are NOT defined in this community module — they live in spreadsheet_edition (enterprise); this module ships only the engine, mixin storage and read-only/public surface.

behavioral_notes.element: data_sources/list/pivot/chart — the ODOO formula engine (client re-evaluation against live models)
behavioral_notes.observation: The 'BI' is data, not Python: cells contain ODOO formulas (ODOO.PIVOT, ODOO.LIST, ODOO.FILTER.VALUE, ODOO.CURRENCY.RATE, charts) re-evaluated client-side. OdooDataProvider (an EventBus) owns the silent ORM + a ServerData batcher that coalesces many cell requests into single read_group/web_search_read RPCs and fires 'data-source-updated' to trigger re-evaluation (debounced, with a 10s safety flush). OdooViewsDataSource (base of ListDataSource and OdooPivotModel) lazily loads field metadata via the field service, recomputes its domain from the live user context + global filters (addDomain/getComputedDomain via @web Domain), and the pivot path (OdooPivot/OdooPivotModel/pivot_time_adapters) reuses @web's pivot_model.js to produce read_group matrices the spreadsheet renders. None of this is reverse-engineerable from Python metadata (gap #3); a dashboard/document is a stored workbook whose figures are computed in the browser.

behavioral_notes.element: FRONTEND (gap #3, STRONG) — the o-spreadsheet OWL engine + public read-only app
behavioral_notes.observation: The substance of this module is a massive OWL/JS application in static/src: ~100 JS files / 15 XML, fronted by the bundled @odoo/o-spreadsheet library (o_spreadsheet/o_spreadsheet.js) wrapped by OdooSpreadsheetModel (model.js) and the SpreadsheetComponent action root (actions/spreadsheet_component.js). It contributes the full Odoo layer ON TOP of the generic grid: data_sources/, pivot/, list/, chart/ (odoo_chart, odoo_menu, geo charts via chartjs-chart-geo + treemap libs), global_filters/ (date/relation/text/numeric filter plugins + components), ir_ui_menu/ (clickable cells that open Odoo views/menus via odoo_menu_link_cell), helpers/ (migration.js workbook version migrations, geo_json_service, freezeOdooData which snapshots a live workbook into a frozen/static copy by evaluating every ODOO cell to a literal value and rasterizing odoo charts to PNG), logging/, and print_assets/. A separate public_readonly_app/ boots its own standalone OWL App (main.js -> PublicReadonlySpreadsheet) from a dedicated spreadsheet.public_spreadsheet bundle (52 includes: its own bootstrap/bootstrap-css + a trimmed web core) so a frozen spreadsheet can render on a public portal page with no web client. Registry: actions:action_download_spreadsheet, fields:binary_spreadsheet, services:geo_json_service + spreadsheetLinkMenuCell. Patches: Grid/Spreadsheet prototypes and several chart components. This frontend is the product; the 1 route + 1 abstract model + 5 thin helper extensions are a thin server skirt around it.

classification.rationale: spreadsheet is firm-infrastructure / BI-tooling (Porter support activity; Stabell & Fjeldstad 'support'). It creates no primary value in any single value chain/shop/network — it is a horizontal analytics-and-document engine reused across apps: every concrete spreadsheet record (dashboards, documents, templates, BI pivots) inherits its spreadsheet.mixin storage contract and renders through its OWL o-spreadsheet client. Its substance is overwhelmingly the FRONTEND (~100 JS files: the wrapped o-spreadsheet library, the Odoo data_sources/pivot/list/chart layer that re-evaluates ODOO formulas against live models, global filters, ir.ui.menu link cells, freeze/export, and a standalone public read-only app) plus a thin server skirt: 1 abstract model, 1 telemetry route, and 5 read-only helper extensions (lang/currency/model). APQC 13.0 'Develop and Manage Business Capabilities' is chosen because this module delivers the self-service business-intelligence / analytics-spreadsheet capability the organization uses to measure and improve its other capabilities — it is performance-measurement/decision-support tooling, a business-capability concern sitting on top of the IT platform. 8.0 'Manage Information Technology' was considered (it is platform/runtime code, like `web`) but rejected: unlike `web` — a generic UI runtime that is pure IT delivery with no business semantics — spreadsheet's purpose is data-bound analytics (pivots/lists/charts over business models, KPI dashboards, frozen reports) consumed for decision-making, which is business-intelligence tooling (13.0) rather than IT delivery itself. The sibling spreadsheet_dashboard record is classified identically (support / 13.0).

common_gaps: Collaborative real-time editing (dispatch_spreadsheet_message / save_spreadsheet_snapshot / revisions) is NOT in this community module — it ships in spreadsheet_edition (enterprise)
Authoring workbook content / ODOO formulas is data-modeling work, not config (requires the editor + understanding of the target models)
Custom OWL components, new chart types, or new ODOO formula functions require JS dev against the o-spreadsheet engine (gap #3)
No external/BI-integration surface here (gap #7) — 0 HTTP call sites, no SDKs/api-keys; all data stays inside Odoo via call_kw
